reason: H0 exclusively builds and exercises the JSON decoder and auxiliary JSON API, while S1 exposes a new std/webp decoder implementing base.image_decoder. Consequently, none of the WebP decoder entry points or its call-sequence and restart protocol are reached. This is material even though the current implementation is minimal because externally controlled call ordering, source state, nullable outputs, restart arguments, pixel-buffer/work-buffer parameters, and closed-versus-streaming input behavior define a distinct fuzzable API surface.
evidence: H0 defines WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__JSON and WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__AUX__JSON but no WEBP or VP8 module.
H0 calls wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson; it never constructs or invokes a webp.decoder.
S1 declares pub struct decoder? implements base.image_decoder with call_sequence and frame_config_io_position state.

decoder.decode_image_config?, decoder.decode_frame_config?, and decoder.decode_frame? expose separate stateful entry points using base.io_reader and convert a short read on a closed source to #truncated input.
decoder.do_decode_frame_config? branches on call_sequence values 0x20, 0x28, 0x40, and other states, including #bad restart and @end of data outcomes.
decoder.restart_frame! accepts attacker-variable index and io_position, checks them against frame_config_io_position, and transitions call_sequence to 0x28.
decoder.decode_frame? accepts a pixel buffer, blend mode, workbuf slice, and nullable decode_frame_options, none of which H0 varies or exercises.
recommended_action: Add a dedicated WebP image-decoder harness that enables the WEBP and VP8 modules, feeds arbitrary and incrementally limited base.io_reader input, and generates valid and invalid sequences across decode_image_config?, decode_frame_config?, decode_frame?, restart_frame!, and tell_me_more?. Vary closed/streaming source state, nullable destination/options arguments, restart index and io_position, pixel-buffer configuration, blend values, and work-buffer sizes while checking status, progress, counters, and call-sequence invariants.
